subject: chemistry

hotspots.label: Neutrons in the nucleus
hotspots.description: The gray particles packed in the dense core are the neutrons — the silent partners of the protons in the nucleus.
hotspots.positionHint: The cluster of gray spheres at the center of the cutaway.
hotspots.function: Shows the neutrons packed in the atom's nucleus.

hotspots.label: Zero charge
hotspots.description: Unlike the protons, the neutrons carry no charge marker — they are electrically neutral, adding mass but no charge.
hotspots.positionHint: The gray neutrons standing apart from the charged protons.
hotspots.function: Shows that the neutron has no electric charge.

hotspots.label: Isotope pair
hotspots.description: Two carbon atoms side by side: one with 6 neutrons, one with 8. Same protons, same element — different neutron counts make isotopes.
hotspots.positionHint: The two atom pairs below, visible when the isotope layer is on.
hotspots.function: Shows how neutron count varies between isotopes.

visualStyleNotes: Chemistry palette, Anatomy Atelier bar: warm off-white/paper background (#F7F3EC) with a soft radial vignette, no floor grid, no props. A cutaway nucleus floats centered, lit with soft neutral studio light — no rim-light glow, no bloom, no emissive anywhere. Clean stylized product-render look, specimen-quality not cartoon. Nucleus: soft muted gray neutrons and soft red protons bundled together, one quadrant cut away; a faint translucent warm-white electron-cloud shell surrounds it. Strong saturated color is reserved for the small flat hotspot dots and the isotope highlight (slate / amber / molecular-green accents from the Chemistry palette). Slow auto-rotation, calm, minimal chrome.
materialNotes: Metallic-roughness PBR, metallic=0 everywhere, single 2K shared texture atlas. Neutrons: soft muted gray spheres, roughness ~0.4. Protons: soft muted red spheres, roughness ~0.4. Electron cloud: large translucent warm-white shell, alpha ~0.12. No emissive channels anywhere — any glow is handled by app runtime UI.
assetBrief:
SUBJECT: a nucleus cutaway focused on the neutron, built to be read as 'the charge-free particle that adds mass and makes isotopes.' Three procedural layers, all clean primitives:

1) MAIN: a cutaway nucleus cluster at center — ~6 soft muted gray neutron spheres (radius ~0.22) and ~6 soft muted red proton spheres (radius ~0.22) packed together with one quadrant cut away; a faint translucent warm-white electron-cloud shell (radius ~1.5, alpha ~0.12) surrounds it with a gap.

2) MASS COMPARE (toggleable layer): a small translucent teal electron dot appears far out at the cloud edge (radius ~0.06) — the app renders a balance or scale hint contrasting the heavy nucleus with the nearly weightless electron.

3) ISOTOPES (toggleable layer): two small carbon atom icons appear side by side below — each a tiny nucleus (6 red protons) with one showing 6 gray neutrons and the other 8 (app highlights the differing neutrons in amber).

Camera: framed so the nucleus is clearly visible within the cloud; auto-rotate default. Budget 6-10k triangles. Named nodes: NucleusCluster, Neutrons_06, Protons_06, ElectronCloud, CutawayPlane, MassElectron, Isotope_12, Isotope_14, IsotopeNeutronsExtra. All labels are hotspot dots in the app layer.
